answer: For an exchange of umber pigments, nectar forecasts and nebula images, mint a nontransferable earning permit only after a key destroys a fixed fee. A burn transaction names the key and epoch; validators count each output once and refuse expired permits. A thousand aliases therefore destroy a thousand fees even if operated simultaneously. Set the fee above the expected extra per-key subsidy. This relies on final burn accounting and realistic reward estimates; rich attackers can pay, and newcomers face the same fee.
